changelog:
Corrects a packaging fault in 1.9.4. The dashboard carried inside the data file was stamped with a version five releases old, while the copy published on the web carried the right one, so the two were not the identical files 1.9.4 said they were. Everything in 1.9.4 works; this makes the two copies genuinely the same, and adds a check that fails the build if they ever diverge again.

1.9.4 itself brought the following, and all of it stands:

The Experience card tracks base and job separately. Each has its own percentage, its own current and required exp, its own remaining count and its own time to level, because they advance at different rates and one of them is often already at its cap.

A level at its cap now reads MAX. The server reports "no next level" as a requirement of nine hundred quadrillion, and taken at face value that produced a bar stuck at 0.00%, a remaining count in the quintillions and a time to level of roughly 381 million years.

The dashboard served on your own PC is now the same dashboard published on the web. There used to be a separate, older copy built into the program, so a phone on the public page and a browser on the overlay's address were running different software. The app manifest, the service worker and the app icon all differed too.

The dashboard travels in the data file rather than inside the program, so improvements to it can be delivered as a small data update instead of a whole new download.
